craft_notes: Sthāyin: knife-joy (the cutting praised). Sanskrit first: knot named, knife praised, morsel stated → L4 keeps all three uncut, colon lands the devouring. Rows: row 2 (the knife-image whole line 1 — never split). Rupture: colon after blade — instrument held, work stated. Close: end-weight on devouring (stillness eaten). Minimal pass: 'it ate up' for 'made morsel' (same devouring, sung). Read aloud: name, knife, swallow. Rejected: 'sword' — killed: kṛpāṇikā is knife (small, surgical); 'both motion and rest' — killed: throb/stillness kept blunt.

lines: I bow — I — to pure awareness, sole knife-blade
for the heart-knot of mine-and-I: it ate up throb and stillness.
l4.sanskrit_cite: mamāham iti hṛdgranthicchedanaikakṛpāṇikām / spandāspandakṛtagrāsāṃ naumy ahaṃ śuddhasaṃvidam

reads_against.argmap: I bow to pure awareness: sole knife for the mine-I heart-knot, devourer of throb and throbless.
c1_essence: I bow to pure awareness: sole knife for the mine-I knot.
